---
title: "Getting Started with Age-Structured Models"
format: html
---

This tutorial shows the core `agepi` design pattern: define an age structure,
build a long-form compartment-by-age state, attach a recipient-by-source
contact matrix, simulate an SIR model, and inspect the result with compact
summary helpers.

It is a small research prototype, not a calibrated study. For a broader
overview, see [README.md](../README.md), [docs/epidemic_model_workflows.md](../docs/epidemic_model_workflows.md),
[docs/model_conventions.md](../docs/model_conventions.md), and
[examples/mock_sir_deterministic.R](../examples/mock_sir_deterministic.R).

```{r}
if ("package:agepi" %in% search()) {
  # Package already available.
} else if (dir.exists("R")) {
  invisible(lapply(list.files("R", pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE), source))
} else if (requireNamespace("agepi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(agepi)
} else {
  stop(
    "Package agepi is not available. Run this tutorial from the package root ",
    "or install agepi first.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

age_structure <- AgeStructure(
  age_groups = c("0-4", "5-9", "10-14"),
  lower_bounds = c(0, 5, 10),
  upper_bounds = c(4, 9, 14)
)

population <- c(1000, 1200, 900)
initial_infections <- c(5, 3, 2)

initial_state <- data.frame(
  compartment = rep(c("S", "I", "R"), each = age_structure$n_age_groups),
  age_group = rep(age_structure$age_groups, times = 3),
  value = c(population - initial_infections, initial_infections, rep(0, 3)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

contact_matrix <- matrix(
  c(
    4, 2, 1,
    2, 5, 2,
    1, 2, 4
  ),
  nrow = age_structure$n_age_groups,
  byrow = TRUE
)

model <- SIRModel(gamma = 0.25)

simulation <- simulate_deterministic(
  initial_state = initial_state,
  times = seq(0, 10, by = 1),
  model = model,
  age_structure = age_structure,
  contact_matrix = contact_matrix,
  beta = 0.08
)

head(simulation, 12)
compartment_totals(simulation)
age_group_totals(simulation)
total_population(simulation)
```

The state is long form, so each row represents one compartment-age cell. The
contact matrix uses recipient rows and source columns, which keeps the mixing
convention explicit and inspectable.

The summary helpers are useful for quick checks:

- `compartment_totals()` shows how each compartment evolves;
- `age_group_totals()` shows the age profile at each time;
- `total_population()` gives a simple aggregate population trajectory.

If you want more detail on how the age-grid convention works, return to
[docs/model_conventions.md](../docs/model_conventions.md). For a fuller
walkthrough of the epidemic workflow, see
[docs/epidemic_model_workflows.md](../docs/epidemic_model_workflows.md).
